summary: PR 2617 is valid test-only hardening: its exact candidate passes on the assigned gfx950 and its GPU regression now rejects a blocking D2H mutation. It does not change production code or independently prove the TP8 H200 near-full-KV hang is resolved.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact candidate c6a20683551a8513301dd49d93c12cf78494683f: 4 passed, covering direct and helper-indirected host-conversion guards plus empty and populated real-GPU D2H results.

tests.command: Temporarily mutate managers.utils._async_d2h to copy_(..., non_blocking=False), then run pytest -q test/registered/spec/test_eagle_verify_result_d2h.py -k async_pinned_d2h
tests.what_was_measured: Both GPU parameter cases failed at the explicit non_blocking=True assertion; the mutation was restored immediately.

tests.command: Run the candidate AST algorithm on module-local sync_helper, alias = sync_helper, and run_eagle_verify calling alias
tests.what_was_measured: The scanner returned no forbidden conversion, demonstrating an alias-indirection boundary not covered by the static guard.

gpu_execution.evidence: Real ROCm tensors, pinned host allocations, D2H copies, event synchronization, and exact values ran on HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0, AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950.

remaining_counterexamples: A module-local alias to a helper containing Tensor.tolist()/cpu()/numpy() bypasses the candidate AST scanner; imported helpers and dynamic dispatch are also outside its scope.
The production hang may still depend on TP8 coordination, CUDA/H200 behavior, GLM-5.1 FP8 execution, or near-full KV/memory pressure, none of which this environment can exercise.
remaining_limitations: Only one AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950 with ROCm 7.2 was assigned, not eight H200 CUDA GPUs.
The original synchronous tolist failure is already absent on recorded base 358c163250ad3b1f62939b01ce1314a0a31a0365, so failing-before production reproduction on that prepared base was impossible.
No native source changed; native rebuild was not applicable.
